messages:
Nora: Pulled together a tiny playbook for 'consent escrow' fallback. Resident region preferred; if it's unhealthy we may forward to an escrow pool *only* when tenant provided explicit consent token. Proposal below.

Sam: Love the principle. Quick question: should the token be tenant-scoped or tenant+model-scoped? Model pins complicate fallback.

Nora: Tenant+model-scoped seems safer. Token payload: tenant_id, allowed_regions, allowed_features (e.g., no_tools, max_tokens=256), model_whitelist, exp. Signed by control-plane KMS key.

Priya: Ops: enforce admission control w/ per-tenant concurrency budget and global pool capacity. If budget exhausted, return a deterministic 429 with header X-Fallback-Reason: capacity. Avoid silent fallback.

Jules: Product: add a UI toggle and checkbox with contract text. Also surface a knob to constrain degraded feature set per tenant.

ops-bot: ops-bot: reminder: canary schedule requested for escrow-pool:v1.2 on 2024-06-20T01:00Z

Sam: Observability: emit fallback_granted{tenant,region}, fallback_denied{reason}, fallback_latencies. Also tag traces with residency_assertion_id. That helps audits.

Priya: Important infra constraint: escrow pool must not cache or persist model weights across tenants. Use ephemeral per-request mounts or strict memory isolation.

Nora: Failure modes we considered: (1) token replay across regions -> mitigate by single-use nonce + short TTL; (2) model mismatch -> runtime consults mapping table and returns code FBACK_MODEL_MISMATCH with suggested compatible models; (3) sudden surge -> admission controller + soft-degrade.

Jules: Legal already asked that any cross-region inference be logged with tenant consent snapshot. So include assertion_id + signed_claim in audit logs. Also surface opt-out in billing UI.

Priya: Action items: Nora write minimal RFC for token schema + verification (due Mon), Sam add fallback metrics + trace tags (due Tue), Ops validate admission controller prototype under chaos (due Wed), Jules wire product toggle + docs (due Thu).

Nora: One more dev example for local testing:
```
curl -H "X-Residency-Assertion: eyJhbGciOiJSU..." \
  -H "X-Residency-Mode: escrow" \
  https://inference.redwood/v1/respond -d '{"prompt":"status?"}'
```

Sam: No blockers from infra side. We'll also add an alert when fallback_granted > 0.5% of traffic for a tenant in 5m.

Jules: I'll draft the customer FAQ language: what happens, how to opt-in/out, and expected degraded capabilities.

Nora: Thanks all. I'll post the RFC link here when ready and include a tiny JSON schema for the token. Ping me for review.
